newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Sept consumer prices down 0.4 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Sept consumer prices down 0.4 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Consumer prices in the Tokyo area in September dropped by 0.4 percent from a year ago, while nationwide consumer prices in August rose 0.2 percent from a year ago, the government's Management and Coordination Agency said on Friday.
Overall Tokyo prices minus fresh food prices or core prices, a key barometer for gauging core inflation, dropped 0.3 percent in September from a year earlier.
An agency official told a media briefing that Tokyo prices were on a stable trend on both a year-on-year and month-on-month basis.

An official at the government's Economic Planning Agency told the same briefing that he had initially thought prices of fresh vegetables or fish might have fallen this time because of the O-157 bacteria food-poisoning epidemic which swept the nation this summer. But in reality, he added, he could not detect any major impact from the epidemic.

The threat of the killer bacteria led to some declines in radish sprout prices, but overall, nationwide fresh food prices posted a smaller year-on-year increase in August mainly because of a good harvest of cabbages and tomatoes this year, he said.
"Domestic prices are on a stable trend," the official said.
